title: Stability Gate: Routing and KMS Handshake
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on network handshake stability, KMS integration for private deployment, and routing fallback tests. Team validated kernel upgrade schedule, agreed to run an end-to-end PSK + mTLS handshake test, and requested Redwood security pack + KMS playbook. Action items captured and a canary bench scheduled next week.
next_steps: Redwood to send KMS integration playbook and security packet (Lara) - 2025-09-19
Customer to run handshake test using test vectors and share logs (Priya) - 2025-09-22
Schedule 90-min canary benchmark with sample traffic (Marco + Evan) - target 2025-09-24
Agree rollback window for kernel upgrade (Hannah, Marco) - 2025-09-23
action_items: Lara Chen: share KMS + HSM integration doc and cipher list by 2025-09-19
Marco Ruiz: draft handshake test harness and sample scripts by 2025-09-18
Priya Nair: run PSK + mTLS handshake test and upload logs to shared folder by 2025-09-22
Hannah Lee: confirm kernel upgrade maintenance window and rollback snapshot by 2025-09-23
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Tanya Singh (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Aegis NetOps), Jamal Ortiz (Aegis Sec), Hannah Lee (Aegis Cloud Eng), Evan Brooks (Aegis ML Infra)

Auto-summary (auto): quick status, handshake failures on week 4, KMS key wrapping questions, plan to run bench and canary.

[00:00] Lara Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we good on time?
[00:07] Priya Nair: Yep, good here, thanks Lara. Sorry running a little late cause a deploy earlier.
[00:12] Lara Chen: No worries, we can cover the kernel bit later. Marco, do you want to kick us off with telemetry?
[00:18] Marco Ruiz: Sure. So quick recap from last week: we saw intermittent handshake failures between the private control plane and the on-prem worker nodes, primarily during concurrent canary bursts. We traced a majority to a PSK negotiation timeout, some to TLS session renegotiation, and a small subset to a routing flap when the egress path switched.
[00:40] Jamal Ortiz: Right, and from our side we saw the same; some cert chaining looked odd in the logs, looked like a partial chain under heavy CPU. Might be a threadpool starvation in the mux.
[00:52] Hannah Lee: There's also the KMS wrap/unwrap calls which spiked and increased latency on the key service. We need to be careful not to overload our HSM during canary.
[01:05] Marco Ruiz: Exactly. So we've got three threads: one, make the handshake deterministic under burst; two, make the KMS interaction async-ish and backoff; three, ensure routing fallback sequencing doesn't interrupt active sessions.
[01:20] Priya Nair: For determinism, can we force session resumption policies or cache the early material?
[01:25] Marco Ruiz: We can. Redwood runtime supports prefix KV cache and session caching — we can bump the TTL for handshake material for the pilot nodes. That reduces full handshake rate by roughly 40% in our lab.
[01:36] Evan Brooks: Are there any side effects for multi-tenant noise? I know this is private but still want to know if caching increases memory or KV pressure.
[01:42] Marco Ruiz: Good point. In private deployment the KV cache lives on the node and we've seen a modest memory bump — like 150MB per worker in our test config. For your scale it's acceptable, but if you want we can tune per-pool.
[01:56] [TRANSCRIBER NOTE: brief crosstalk]
[02:01] Lara Chen: Ok, KMS. Jamal, you raised a question last week about key caching vs HSM load, can you restate?
[02:07] Jamal Ortiz: Yeah, our compliance team doesn't want long key caching windows — they prefer short TTLs with frequent HSM ops to keep auditability tight. But the HSM we've got has limited ops/sec, so under a spike we hit queuing.
[02:23] Marco Ruiz: So a suggestion: Redwood supports optional KMS proxy layer that batches wrap/unwrap and retries with jitter. We also support hardware keywrap with customer-provided HSM through the KMS plugin. The tradeoff is audit granularity vs latency/cost.
[02:38] Hannah Lee: Is that proxy managed in your control plane or in our VPC? We need it to be in VPC for us.
[02:44] Lara Chen: For Private, the KMS proxy can be deployed in customer VPC; Redwood provides the image and the playbook.
[02:51] Priya Nair: Cool. Could that proxy implement a token bucket so we don't overload the HSM?
[02:57] Marco Ruiz: Yes, token-bucket and exponential backoff, and we can surface metrics via the telemetry endpoint so you'll see when we're rate limiting.
[03:06] Lara Chen: Great. Next, routing fallback sequence — we had that weird flip where traffic moved to fallback and dropped active sessions. Marco, is that from the controller order?
[03:15] Marco Ruiz: In the current pilot default, fallback policy does an immediate route swap which can cause in-flight connection resets for long-polling sessions. We have a graceful handoff mode that drains existing connections first then switches. It adds 300-800ms to failover but avoids resets.
[03:31] Priya Nair: Drain mode sounds better for us; we have several long-running inference calls. 800ms is fine compared to resets.
[03:37] Evan Brooks: Does drain mode increase tail latency during failover?
[03:40] Marco Ruiz: Slightly, you'll see some queued requests, but it's preferable to failed requests. We can also do hybrid: fast-fail for low-criticality routes, drain for critical routes.
[03:50] Hannah Lee: Can we map certain endpoint tags to drain vs fast-fail?
[03:53] Marco Ruiz: Yep, route policy supports tags and per-route SLOs. We'll include a sample policy in the playbook.
[03:59] [00:04:04] Lara Chen: Kernel upgrade window — we scheduled it Tuesday night, but customer asked for a narrower window. Hannah?
[04:10] Hannah Lee: We have a maintenance window on Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Our ops lead wants a 30-minute rollback period and snapshot in place.
[04:18] Marco Ruiz: Redwood's runtime upgrade includes a canary roll where we patch 2 nodes first, run health probes for 10 minutes, then roll. If health fails we auto-rollback. We can tighten the probe and shorten canary to 5 minutes if you want but increases risk.
[04:31] Priya Nair: Auto-rollback is necessary. Also want a playbook for manual rollback steps and verification commands.
[04:38] Marco Ruiz: We'll share the rollback runbook with commands and expected outputs.
[04:42] Lara Chen: Back to handshake test plan — Marco, you proposed a harness last week. Status?
[04:47] Marco Ruiz: I have a draft harness that runs 1k concurrent short-lived session attempts and 200 long-lived sessions. It emits a test vector of PSK+cert and captures the trace. I can push it to the shared folder later today.
[04:59] Evan Brooks: Please include the log redaction rules — we can't send raw PII or cert material.
[05:04] Marco Ruiz: Absolutely, we'll redact cert private material and provide clear instructions for what to scrub.
[05:09] Priya Nair: When we run this harness, which environment should we use? Staging or canary?
[05:13] Lara Chen: Start in staging but maintain a near-prod canary to validate scale. For the handshake failures we want both.
[05:19] Jamal Ortiz: Also, security wants a brief threat model doc for the handshake flow, specifically around PSK fallback and replay windows.
[05:27] Lara Chen: We'll include a short threat model and the mitigations we have in place (nonce freshness, AEAD, sequence numbers).
[05:34] [TRANSCRIBER NOTE: minor word substitution: "nonce" transcribed as "nouns"]
[05:40] Hannah Lee: Telemetry gaps: we don't see per-token latency distribution in the panel right now; we only get 95/99 on route. Can we add per-request token histograms?
[05:49] Marco Ruiz: We can. Redwood Console supports token-level tracing for pilot retention; it's off by default due to volumes but we can enable a sampling rate and surface histograms. That will help root cause tail latency.
[06:02] Priya Nair: Sampling might miss intermittent spikes. Could we do an adaptive sampling triggered by circuit-breaker events?
[06:09] Marco Ruiz: Yes, adaptive sampling is in the runtime — it increases sampling when error rate or latency breach occurs. We'll flip that on for the pilot.
[06:18] Lara Chen: Ok, align on deliverables: security packet + KMS playbook, handshake harness, canary bench. Anything else?
[06:25] Jamal Ortiz: One more: SSO/SAML mapping for RBAC. Our Okta team needs role mapping examples for Redwood service accounts.
[06:33] Lara Chen: We'll send SSO mapping examples and a sample RBAC policy.
[06:36] Tanya Singh: Also I'll follow up with a short runbook for on-call escalation to Redwood SEs during the bench window.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Great. A question on pricing: if we move KMS calls to proxy and it's in our VPC, is there an extra Redwood charge?
[06:53] Lara Chen: For Private deployments the KMS proxy is included in the platform fee for pilot; for production we'll discuss usage-based pass-through for HSM operations. We'll note pricing in the packet.
[07:03] Evan Brooks: Competitor note: VendorX charged extra for HSM proxy, just flagging.
[07:08] Lara Chen: Noted.
[07:10] [00:07:12] Marco Ruiz: Quick technical note: during the kernel patch we found a regression for KV cache eviction which caused a small memory leak under one test. Patch 1.2.3 fixes it, we recommend applying patch before the upgrade.
[07:25] Hannah Lee: Can we get the patch SHA and a short test plan?
[07:28] Marco Ruiz: Yes: SHA abc123... (audio: abc one two three), I'll drop the exact SHA and test script in the folder.
[07:36] Priya Nair: For the handshake logs, we might share sanitized PCAPs. Is that ok?
[07:41] Lara Chen: That's fine but if PCAP includes PII we ask you to redact. We'll provide a redaction checklist.
[07:48] [TRANSCRIBER NOTE: occasional filler words and sentence fragments remain]
[07:53] Jamal Ortiz: On audit logs — we need to confirm retention policy and access paths for KMS ops. Our compliance wants 7 years of wrap/unwrap audit trails.
[08:03] Lara Chen: Redwood stores rich audit logs in the control plane by default; for Private we can stream audit events to your SIEM via our log forwarder. We have references for long-term retention patterns.
[08:16] Hannah Lee: Will those be encrypted at rest with our key?
[08:19] Lara Chen: Yes, if you use your KMS we can wrap logs with your key before storing or forwarding.
[08:25] Priya Nair: Ok action items seem clear. Let's set the bench date now. Lara, you suggested the 24th?
[08:31] Lara Chen: Yes, propose 2025-09-24 UTC 14:00 for a 90-min bench. Everyone ok?
[08:36] Priya Nair: Works for us.
[08:38] Jamal Ortiz: Works.
[08:39] Hannah Lee: I'll block it.
[08:41] Evan Brooks: I'll prep the sample workload.
[08:43] Lara Chen: Great. Final recap: Redwood sends KMS playbook + security packet + SSO mapping + kernel patch SHA and handshake harness today/tomorrow; Aegis runs handshake tests and uploads logs; bench scheduled 2025-09-24 14:00 UTC.
[08:57] Marco Ruiz: I'll also include a short route policy example for drain vs fast-fail and a sample adaptive sampling config.
[09:04] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[09:05] Tanya Singh: I'll follow up with calendar invite and the escalation runbook.
[09:09] Lara Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after bench or sooner if issues.
[09:13] Priya Nair: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
